question.problem: Consider the function $f(x)=3(x-2)^{3}$ and the point $P(3,3)$ that lies on $y=f(x).$ Given that $f(x)$ is invertible in the vicinity of $P,$  calculate ${({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3).$
question.worked_solution:
We start by calculating the derivative of $f$ at the point $(3,3).$

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}f(x) & =3(x-2)^{3} \\ {f}^{′}(x) & =9(x-2)^{2} \\ {f}^{′}(3) & =9\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Since $(3,3)$ lies on $y=f(x),$ we know that the corresponding point $(3,3)$ lies on $y={f}^{-1}(x).$

Furthermore, the slopes of the tangents to the two respective points are reciprocals. Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\begin{aligned}{({f}^{-1})}^{′}(3) & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}({f}^{-1}(3))} \\  & =\frac{1}{{f}^{′}(3)} \\  & =\frac{1}{9}.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
